question: Does resolving a subtree at decision time (full hand resolution, time budget) improve on a coarse precomputed blueprint, and is it safe?
domain: 52-card river subgames, pot 10, stack 20, bets 50%/100%/all-in, cap 2; blueprint = K strength cells
assumptions: unsafe: opponent range at the subtree root = blueprint reach (opponent assumed to follow the blueprint)
safe: re-solve gadget; opponent may terminate with blueprint counterfactual value per hand (Burch, Johanson & Bowling 2014); guarantee is asymptotic in the re-solve, measured here at finite budgets
resolver's own range = blueprint reach; only the resolver's strategy changes
timing_note: 6 instances ran concurrently; budgets are wall-clock per process; iterations recorded
